claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a presbyter (priest) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem lived in the first half of the fifth century and died c. 450.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was a renowned theologian, biblical commentator, and preacher in the Eastern Church.
Hesychius of Jerusalem served as a priest in the church in Jerusalem c. 412.
Hesychius of Jerusalem composed Homilies 11 and 12 On Lazarus in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
Hesychius probably preached Homily 12 on Lazarus on the Saturday before Palm Sunday at the Lazarion shrine in Bethany (Palestine).

Hesychius' Homily 12, In S. Lazarum, is an artifact of the celebration on the sixth day of the Epiphany octave (Epiphany VI/11 January), when residents of Jerusalem gathered in Bethany and read the account of Jesus' raising of Lazarus.
Epiphany VI had a double significance for the residents of Jerusalem: it commemorated Jesus' birth, but also and even primarily served as the city's primary celebration of the raising of Lazarus.

The celebration on Epiphany VI was the partial continuation of an older and more complex memorial on the Saturday immediately before Holy Week that commemorated all of Jesus' encounter with Mary, the raising of Lazarus, and a later supper shared in the home of Lazarus.
By the mid-fifth century, the church of Jerusalem limited the focus of the older feast to the supper at Lazarus' home and moved the account of Lazarus' raising to Epiphany VI.
The homily survives in manuscript, including in Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Ott. gr. 014, folios 044-046v.
A fragment of Homily 2 also survives and has been identified with CPG 4682 and BHG 2215.
